Definition: A proposed canonical dependency-graph successor built from refreshed deliverable-local dependency registers, holding candidate rows outside the canonical edge register, proposed pending human approval.
The approved legacy dependency graph that supplies the node/path baseline and remains graph authority until DAG-007 approval.
A deliverable-local CSV of dependency edges conforming to the canonical v3.1 schema.
The canonical dependency register schema version every row must declare.
Enum field with allowed values ANCHOR and EXECUTION.
Canonical enum: PREREQUISITE, INTERFACE, HANDOVER, CONSTRAINT, ENABLES, OTHER.
Enum field with allowed values IMPLEMENTS_NODE, TRACES_TO_REQUIREMENT, NOT_APPLICABLE.
A non-authoritative list of CANDIDATE-status dependency rows held outside the canonical active edge register pending human approval.
Kahn-style ordered layers of deliverable nodes computed from the active dependency edge graph.
A strongly connected component (more than one node) in the active edge graph indicating a cycle requiring reconciliation.
The deterministic local merge gate running five evidence surfaces sequentially in F-4-safe order, producing a commit-bound summary artifact.
One evidence surface: an ordered list of commands run sequentially within the sweep.
Deliverable-local lifecycle status file whose Current State value is the lifecycle source of truth for work selection.
The canonical deliverable lifecycle states: OPEN, INITIALIZED, IN_PROGRESS, CHECKING, ISSUED.
A named set of local release checks (skeleton, python, security, cargo, all) planned or executed by check_release_readiness.
Boundary statement that development evidence and dependency refresh do not constitute release claims, professional approval, certification, sealing, authentication, or code-compliance determinations.
